headline: Trump threatens higher tariffs over migrant caravan as Sheinbaum readies China trip
body:
What happened: Donald Trump said he would double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico halts a migrant caravan that left Tapachula, in Chiapas, heading north. President Claudia Sheinbaum responded that no caravan has reached the northern border during Trump's current term and that Mexico will not use force against migrants. The tariff threat comes as Mexico seeks lower U.S. duties on steel, aluminum and vehicles, and Sheinbaum plans to travel to Shenzhen, China, for an APEC business event and a meeting with Xi Jinping, which she says should not complicate talks with Washington.

Separately, the week brought fresh reports that Guillermo Zuany Portillo, a former Chihuahua special prosecutor, aided CIA operations in Mexico in exchange for a U.S. visa, a claim Sheinbaum called significant for the bilateral relationship.

Reported by: Mexico News Daily. Also covered by Reuters, Le Monde, Arab News, El País.

headline: Macron warns cutting Ukraine aid would prolong the fighting
body:
What happened: French President Emmanuel Macron has argued that scaling back support for Ukraine would pave the way for a longer war. His remarks frame continued assistance as a key factor in how the conflict develops. The reporting centres on the risk that reduced backing could strengthen Russia's position on the battlefield, though the full details of the statements could not be checked here.

The comments reflect ongoing European debate over how much military and financial help Kyiv should keep receiving. Macron's position emphasises that aid decisions carry direct consequences for the duration and intensity of the fighting.

Reported by: France 24. Also covered by Le Monde, Arab News.

headline: US embassy in Riyadh urges caution as Houthi drone attacks hit Saudi Arabia
body:
What happened: The US embassy in Riyadh has told Americans in the Middle East to stay alert after Iran-backed Houthi forces attacked Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports and key infrastructure, causing civilian deaths and travel disruption. The embassy warned the violence could spread quickly beyond its current area. Separately, Iranian officials reportedly told the New York Times in October that US officials were potential targets, and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he had moved to a military base after credible Iranian assassination threats.

On Saturday the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government said it destroyed two Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh and the southern kingdom. Cross-border fighting has grown as US-Iran tensions rise.

Reported by: Jerusalem Post. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Xinhua.

headline: Israel reportedly lobbies Washington for renewed strikes on Iran
body:
What happened: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly urging US President Donald Trump to restart military attacks on Iran, according to Axios sources. Mossad chief Roman Gofman travelled to Washington, meeting CIA director John Ratcliffe and reportedly planning talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff. The push comes as Netanyahu faces possible loss of power after an election, and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is trying to form a government. Israeli opposition figures worry a new Iran confrontation could be used to delay that transition. Trump has so far favoured sanctions, a naval blockade and possible diplomacy over large-scale strikes.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Jerusalem Post, Xinhua, Fars.

headline: Iraq ships crude by truck to Syria as Hormuz disruption pushes new routes
body:
What happened: Iraq has begun moving heavy crude overland by tanker truck to the Syrian Mediterranean port of Baniyas, a route that had sat largely idle for decades. The shipments, handled by Qatar's UCC Holding under a contract with Iraq's state marketer SOMO, began last month and run at roughly 120,000 to 150,000 barrels per day, depending on truck availability. The effort follows disruption to the Strait of Hormuz caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, and sources told Reuters that Syria's end of years of conflict has also made the route more attractive. Cargoes are then shipped to refineries in Greece, Italy and Turkey, among others.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by Reuters, Arab News.

headline: Yemeni government forces claim hundreds of strikes on Houthi targets
body:
What happened: Yemen's armed forces say they carried out 723 air, drone, rocket and artillery strikes against Houthi positions over a short period, as part of a campaign called "Dawn of Yemen." A military spokesperson said the attacks hit troop concentrations, fortifications, vehicles and equipment on several fronts, including Taiz, Marib, Al-Jawf and southern areas. The spokesperson also claimed around 321 Houthi fighters and commanders were killed or wounded and about 117 vehicles and equipment items destroyed or disabled. These figures are preliminary field estimates from the military and have not been independently verified.

The forces said the campaign aims to counter Houthi threats, including to shipping through the Bab Al-Mandab Strait, and that they would follow international humanitarian law to protect civilians.

Reported by: Arab News. Also covered by Middle East Eye.

headline: Russia reports downing 1,198 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv says Russian strikes hit a hospital
body:
What happened: Russia's defence ministry said it intercepted 1,198 Ukrainian drones overnight across more than 15 regions, a figure it presented as one of the largest such swarms. Four people died at an industrial zone with an oil refinery and chemical plant in Volgograd, local officials said. Ukrainian authorities said Russian overnight attacks set a Kyiv hospital on fire and killed at least three people elsewhere, including in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, with more wounded.

The violence followed US-led shuttle diplomacy aimed at ending the war, which is nearing its fifth year. US envoys met Putin in Moscow and then Zelensky in Dublin. The article also covers Secretary of State Marco Rubio's criticism of the International Criminal Court.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Euronews, Meduza, The Hindu, Buenos Aires Times.

headline: UN calls for fertiliser shipments through Hormuz amid Iran-US standoff
body:
What happened: A senior UN official, Jorge Moreira da Silva of the UN Office for Project Services, asked Iran and the United States on Saturday to immediately let fertiliser cargoes pass through the Strait of Hormuz, even while they keep negotiating a wider deal. He spoke at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Iran's blockade of the waterway, begun after the US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February, and a US blockade of Iranian ports have disrupted shipping. Moreira da Silva said fertiliser prices have risen about 30 percent and warned that missed planting seasons could push tens of millions into hunger and poverty, especially in poorer countries.

Reported by: Al-Monitor. Also covered by Al Jazeera.

headline: EU agrees on a Ukraine negotiating team as Dublin AI summit is overshadowed
body:
What happened: Leaders at an informal EU summit in Dublin spent much of Friday on Ukraine rather than artificial intelligence. They agreed that future peace talks would involve national security advisers from Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland, along with the European Commission and European Council, after disagreement over whether a single envoy should speak for Europe. The concern was a possible US-Russia meeting in Shenzhen on November 18-19, which some European officials fear could settle European security over their heads. Russia's Kremlin said Europeans could join talks only after showing genuine readiness to help the peace process, a condition the EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called a trap.

Reported by: Xinhua. Also covered by The Guardian, Politico Europe, Le Monde, Arab News.

headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six as Hamas and Israel dispute events
body:
What happened: An overnight Israeli air strike hit Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killing six people and wounding about 30, according to the Hamas-run health ministry. Among the dead was surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. The hospital director said two missiles struck a surgical building, though only one exploded, and that the hospital received no warning.

The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas brigade commander and other fighters it claimed were using the hospital as a base, and said it had issued advance warnings. Hamas rejected those claims. Independent verification was difficult because Israel does not allow international media into Gaza.

Reported by: The National. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, NPR, Japan Times.

headline: US senator dismisses further Russia talks after Kremlin demands on NATO troops
body:
What happened: Tom Cotton, the Republican chair of the US Senate Intelligence Committee, has said further negotiations with Russia to end the war are pointless. He was reacting to a Kremlin demand that NATO countries pull their troops back from their own borders, which he described as absurd. Cotton wrote on X that Vladimir Putin has shown he is not serious about a negotiated peace. He argued Putin will only agree to stop fighting once he accepts he cannot win, and said Ukraine should be helped to make that point. The comments were relayed by European Pravda.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, AP, BBC News, The Guardian.

headline: Zelenskyy floats public vote on any security deal with Russia
body:
What happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US envoys raised the idea of Ukraine giving up Donbas in return for NATO membership, following talks in Abu Dhabi. He rejected ceding territory to Russia, but said he would put a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, army funding and reconstruction money, to a public referendum. He also warned that Moscow's push to reshape Europe's security architecture could fuel escalation.

The remarks came as the EU said several European countries, including Germany, France, the UK and Poland, would join future peace talks, something Moscow had opposed. Russia's defence ministry meanwhile claimed the capture of a village in Zaporizhzhia and strikes on Ukrainian energy and military infrastructure.

Reported by: DW. Also covered by OC Media.

headline: ASEAN envoy says Myanmar stance unchanged ahead of Manila summit
body:
What happened: ASEAN's special envoy on Myanmar, Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro, said on Saturday that the bloc is not loosening its approach to Myanmar under the Five-Point Consensus adopted after the 2021 military coup. She told a press conference that a draft review of the framework is still being negotiated and that several proposals will go to leaders. Myanmar's military-backed leaders have been barred from high-level meetings for five years, and Thailand has asked that Myanmar's foreign minister be allowed to attend foreign ministers' meetings. Lazaro said that request remains open for discussion, but no decision has been taken.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by CNA.

headline: Ukraine strikes Russian oil station and airfield deep inside Russian territory
body:
What happened: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces again hit an oil facility in Russia's Samara Oblast, a station that blends crude for the Urals export grade, and reported fires at several storage tanks. It also said the Lipetsk-2 military airfield in Lipetsk Oblast was struck on November 13, with a hangar, an aviation fuel tank and a command post reported hit. The General Staff's claims were not independently verified in this report.

The Samara site is described as a key node in Russia's energy exports, handling oil piped from several regions. Lipetsk-2 is reported to host Su-34, Su-35 and MiG-31 jets.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Reuters, AP, France 24, Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Zelensky says Washington floated Donbas withdrawal for NATO membership
body:
What happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would pull out of the eastern Donbas region in return for joining NATO, a question he says was raised for the first time after recent talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi. He repeated that Kyiv will not give up its territory and said he would consider a referendum only if Ukraine receives a full security package, including guarantees, a strong army and reconstruction funds. Zelensky also warned that Moscow's push to reshape Europe's security order risks further wars, and said the EU and NATO provide the only real security on the continent.

headline: Zelenskyy accuses SpaceX of concealing political motive behind Starshield limits
body:
What happened: Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says SpaceX has been dishonest about why it imposed speed limits on Ukraine's Starshield satellite service, which he argues are political rather than technical. He said the cap of about 100 mph for Ukrainian drones has been in place for five days, cutting off interception of incoming Russian Shahed drones and hampering Ukraine's mid-range strikes on occupied territory. He suggested the restrictions are a US tactic to pressure Kyiv into concessions to Moscow, a claim that could not be independently verified.

Zelenskyy also said US envoys asked whether Ukraine would give up the Donbas in return for NATO membership or NATO-style guarantees, and he rejected Russia's offer of a local humanitarian truce in Kostiantynivka as a tactic to take the city.

Reported by: The Guardian. Also covered by Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: Zelensky says US floated Donbas withdrawal in exchange for Nato membership
body:
What happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says American negotiators have raised the idea of Ukraine pulling its remaining troops out of the eastern Donbas in return for joining Nato. He said this was the first time the proposal had come up, and made the remarks on Saturday after US envoys met him in Dublin following talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Zelensky added that he would put any offer with security guarantees and rebuilding funds to a referendum, while warning that Putin's signals suggest a very difficult discussion ahead.

Russia continues to demand territory and neutrality from Ukraine, which Kyiv rejects. Russia holds roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donbas.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by BBC News, Politico Europe, Sky News, Asharq Al-Awsat.

headline: US senator dismisses further Russia talks after Kremlin demands on NATO troops
body:
What happened: Tom Cotton, the Republican chair of the US Senate Intelligence Committee, has said further negotiations with Russia to end the war are pointless. He was reacting to a Kremlin demand that NATO countries pull their troops back from their own borders, which he described as absurd. Cotton wrote on X that Vladimir Putin has shown he is not serious about a negotiated peace. He argued Putin will only agree to stop fighting once he accepts he cannot win, and said Ukraine should be helped to make that point. The comments were relayed by European Pravda.

Reported by: Le Monde. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Arab News, Kyiv Independent.

headline: Estonia details drone strike on Russian corvette near Ust-Luga port
body:
What happened: Estonian Colonel Aron Kalmus, deputy commander of the Estonian Division, described how several Ukrainian drones hit the Russian Baltic Fleet corvette Naro-Fominsk during a large attack on the Ust-Luga port. He said the vessel was damaged, reportedly with deaths and injuries, and that it could not continue under its own power. Kalmus also said the drones briefly entered Estonian airspace over the Gulf of Finland and southeastern Estonia, too close to the border to be safely shot down. Ukraine's security service earlier said the ship was struck as part of an operation against oil infrastructure at the port.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Al Jazeera.

headline: Satellite images suggest Saudi Arabia is expanding its missile production site
body:
What happened: Researchers using satellite imagery believe Saudi Arabia is enlarging a ballistic missile plant at al-Duwadimi in Riyadh Province. The expansion is said to aim at larger solid-fuel missiles able to carry heavier payloads over longer distances. The work comes as the kingdom faces intensified missile and drone attacks from Yemen's Houthi movement, which has renewed fighting since July and broken a UN-brokered truce in place since 2022. The Houthis say they are responding to a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in areas they control. Analysts quoted by the outlet say the confrontation has raised the importance of Saudi Arabia's missile arsenal.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Reuters, The New Arab, Jerusalem Post, Dawn.

headline: US responds to suspected drone flight over Lakenheath base in England
body:
What happened: US forces answered a possible unauthorised drone sighting above RAF Lakenheath on Friday, American and British officials said. The US Air Force said no personnel, aircraft or facilities were harmed, and Britain's Ministry of Defence said the matter was resolved. The episode follows US charges against three men described as Iranian operatives over an alleged September plot at RAF Fairford, and US aircraft have been moved from other British bases amid Iranian threats tied to the regional war.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Reuters, AP, The Guardian, Le Monde.

headline: Russian strikes kill three and wound seven across three Ukrainian regions
body:
What happened: Russian attacks over the past day in Kherson, Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk oblasts killed three people and injured seven, according to regional military administrations. In Kherson Oblast, two people were killed and five hurt as infrastructure and residential areas were hit, damaging apartment blocks, houses, a post office and an ambulance. In Dnipropetrovsk's Nikopol district, forces reportedly struck nearly ten times with drones and artillery, injuring two people, while one person died in Yasna Poliana in Donetsk Oblast.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Reuters, SCMP, Kyiv Independent.

headline: Türkiye and Qatar agree mutual defence pact in Istanbul
body:
What happened: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan and Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, signed a mutual defence agreement at Dolmabahce Palace in Istanbul on Friday. Turkey's presidency said the two leaders aimed to prevent a renewed outbreak of war in the Gulf and to build a foundation for dialogue. Erdogan's office described the accord as a new dimension in bilateral ties, but no further details of its terms were released.

Security analyst Yusuf Alabarda, speaking to Al Jazeera, linked the deal to the wider Iran war and to doubts in Gulf states about US security guarantees. He suggested Turkish weapons and air defences could be sent to Qatar in the near term, though this was his assessment rather than an announced plan.

Reported by: The National. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, France 24, Middle East Eye.

headline: Canada and US report progress toward a trade agreement, says Carney
body:
What happened: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said talks between Ottawa and Washington on a trade deal have advanced. The remarks indicate that negotiators have narrowed some differences, though the reporting available does not detail which issues were resolved or when an agreement might be finalised. The update comes amid ongoing tariff tensions between the two neighbours, which have affected cross-border commerce.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Arab News.

headline: Ukraine's General Staff reports new Russian losses in the war
body:
What happened: Ukraine's General Staff said on November 14, 2026 that Russia has lost about 1.62 million troops since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022. The count includes 1,710 Russian casualties recorded over the previous day. The report also lists heavy equipment losses, including thousands of tanks, armored vehicles, artillery systems and aircraft. Ukraine's own losses are not published by its military, and independent estimates from a Western think-tank suggest Russian casualties are considerably higher than Ukraine's.

Reported by: Asharq Al-Awsat. Also covered by Kyiv Independent, Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza, Xinhua.

headline: US downs two Iranian drones after Tehran claims strike on Bahrain radar
body:
What happened: US Central Command says it shot down two one-way attack drones launched by Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Friday, with no injuries or damage reported. The Guard said it had targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an air strike on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran, a claim neither side's account could be independently confirmed. It is the first Iranian-claimed attack on US military assets in a Gulf state since early September, raising fears of renewed conflict. Israel's security cabinet has reportedly ordered preparations for a possible strike on Iran.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, The Guardian, DW.

headline: China's spokesman stresses communication with US military
body:
What happened: China's foreign ministry spokesperson has said Beijing values strategic communication with the US military. The remarks come as speculation mounts over a possible China-US-Russia summit at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen in November, which some have likened to the 1945 Yalta Conference. Analysts quoted in the piece expect little substantive progress, pointing to divergent interests on Ukraine, nuclear arms, trade and AI, while Europe's exclusion from such talks has drawn criticism.

Reported by: BBC News. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, DW, France 24.

headline: Iran claims two tankers burning in Hormuz after striking mines
body:
What happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy says two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines. The IRGC claims the ships had turned off their tracking systems and tried to leave through an unauthorised route while under the protection of US forces. It says the vessels are still burning and have been abandoned, and it released video of the burning ships. The claims come from the Iranian side and could not be independently verified from this report. The IRGC also disputed US military accounts of the incident.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, The National, Arab News.

headline: ICC halts probe into US troops in Afghanistan, refocuses on Taliban
body:
What happened: Judges at the International Criminal Court have ordered an end to investigations into alleged crimes by American forces in Afghanistan, shifting focus to Taliban conduct since 2021. The ruling was made on Thursday but published Friday, citing major obstacles to gathering evidence. The decision also closes the inquiry into the Islamic State affiliate in Khorasan Province. The prosecution says it has already lodged an appeal. The move follows a long dispute between Washington and the court, including US sanctions on ICC staff. The United States is not an ICC member and does not accept its jurisdiction.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, Al-Monitor, The New Arab.

headline: Gulf bloc tells UN Iran has fired thousands of missiles and drones
body:
What happened: Jasem Mohammed Albudaiwi, secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council, told the UN Security Council that Iran has launched more than 7,000 missiles and drones at GCC member states since February 28. He said strikes hit airports, ports, energy sites, power stations, desalination plants and homes across all six members, causing deaths and damage. He also warned that disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is threatening fertilizer supplies and raising famine risks in poorer countries. The GCC holds Tehran fully responsible and called for reparations and action on Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by El País, Arab News, Middle East Eye.
